clue.text: Granted nobody had settled

definitions.meaning: if nobody had paid up, every debt is still outstanding

explanation.surface: A concession made because no one had paid their bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Something granted is permitted; split in two, the word also reads as everything still owed.

clue.text: Complaint found in sloth or South American rodent

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite
gout is a painful complaint of the joints

explanation.surface: An illness turns up in a lazy animal, or perhaps in a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing rodent native to Central and South America.

clue.text: Being behind crime in wood

indicators.note: crime is placed in wood, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: Lagging behind in a forest where some offence has been committed.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is losing is behind in the score.

clue.text: Desolation of writer coming to a head

parts.note: Thornton Wilder was an American writer
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: An author's despair comes to a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' only joins the pieces; 'coming to a head' looks like an idiom but 'a head' is the headland NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is a desolate, uninhabited waste, so the word stands for desolation itself.

clue.text: He wrote of the French missile backfiring

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: a weapon backfiring goes the wrong way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a SAM is a surface-to-air missile

explanation.surface: An account of a French rocket that blew up the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist, so a writer; the definition is a cryptic description of him.

clue.text: Mule managed to get cat out of pipe

indicators.note: the letters are handled and arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mule somehow extracts a cat from a drainpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is the ceremonial tobacco pipe of North American peoples, the peace pipe.

clue.text: Engine cover found by French maid in vehicle

indicators.note: the maid sits in the vehicle, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
bonne is French for a maid

explanation.surface: Something is discovered beside a French housemaid riding in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car bonnet is the hinged panel over a car's engine, called the hood in America.

clue.text: Novice's a person stupid in the head

parts.note: L, for learner, is a novice, as on British L-plates
an oaf is a stupid, clumsy person

explanation.surface: A beginner is a fool, a bit dim in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 's and 'in the' only join; 'use your loaf' is British slang for using your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaf is British slang for the head, from rhyming slang loaf of bread.

clue.text: Name for publication composed in mad haste

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a fresh arrangement, as type is composed

explanation.surface: A newspaper title written in a frantic hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title of a newspaper printed at the top of its front page.

clue.text: Staying behind and endeavouring to get round rising artist

indicators.note: one piece gets round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: trying means endeavouring

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, trying to win over an up-and-coming painter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the artist upwards before 'to get round' wraps the endeavouring word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarrying means lingering or delaying, staying behind rather than leaving.

clue.text: Bird of tremendous eloquence

indicators.note: the bird is made of letters drawn from the run of words

explanation.surface: A bird of remarkable eloquence, like a talking parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird or the ring ouzel, a thrush.

clue.text: Diver finding short answer in business combine

indicators.note: the shortened answer goes in the business deal, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a merger is a combination of businesses
ANS is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: Someone diving into a company merger to find a brief reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A merganser is a fish-eating duck that dives for its prey.

clue.text: Pressure undesirable here, so offers drugs

parts.note: tenders means offers
pot is cannabis, a drug

explanation.surface: A pusher offers drugs, and pressure would be unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender spot is a sore place where any pressure hurts, so pressure there is unwelcome.

clue.text: How he yearns to discover a milk product

indicators.note: the answer is there to be discovered within the run of words

explanation.surface: How a man longs to find some dairy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery part of milk left when curds form in cheese-making.

clue.text: Give the boy a wash and a biscuit

definitions.meaning: bath is to wash someone, and Oliver is a boy's name
a plain hard biscuit created in the English city of Bath by Dr Oliver

explanation.surface: Wash a boy, then hand him a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is a dry, unsweetened biscuit named for the Bath physician William Oliver.

clue.text: Sometimes it is no advantage to include a girl

indicators.note: one piece includes the other, which sits inside it

parts.note: no gain means no advantage
Wanda is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Sometimes inviting a girl along brings no benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is' and 'a' are only link words; the girl's name splits the phrase for no advantage between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and again means occasionally, from time to time, so it is synonymous with sometimes.

clue.text: Watch a wise man in aftermath of blitz

parts.note: to ward is to guard or watch over
a mage is a magus, a wise man

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a sage amid the ruins of a bombing raid.
explanation.definitionFit: War damage is destruction caused by fighting, such as the bombed buildings left after the Blitz on British cities.

clue.text: Arrangement of flowers in the pit

definitions.meaning: a formal garden of patterned flower beds
in a theatre, the ground-floor seats behind the orchestra

explanation.surface: A floral display set in the theatre stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is both a formal patterned garden and, especially in America, the theatre pit.

clue.text: Injured child exposed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
aired means exposed to view or to air

explanation.surface: A hurt youngster laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, as something injured is.

clue.text: Penalty for a gunrunning exercise?

parts.note: an arms dealer's prison sentence is a stretch for arms, and stretching the arms is a physical exercise

explanation.surface: A gun smuggler is sentenced, or someone does a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the reach of an arm, and also reads as a stretch (jail term) for arms trafficking.

clue.text: Change over to a rod

definitions.meaning: to swap one thing for another
a thin flexible stick used as a whip

explanation.surface: Swapping to a fishing rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Switch means to change over, and also a slender cane or rod.

clue.text: Tell Doris, perhaps

definitions.meaning: William Tell, the legendary Swiss bowman who shot an apple off his son's head
Doris was a matriarch in the long-running British radio soap about a farming family in Ambridge

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell Doris something.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell was a famous bowman, and Doris was a character of that surname in the BBC radio soap The Archers.

clue.text: Hidden danger in role reversal

indicators.note: a reversal turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A concealed risk when actors swap roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a concealed hazard set to catch the unwary.

clue.text: Spectator at dance often goes to bed

definitions.meaning: someone who stays by the wall at a dance, watching but not dancing
a garden plant commonly bedded out in flower beds

explanation.surface: A shy dancer who watches, then leaves early to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a shy person left out at a dance and also a fragrant spring bedding plant.

clue.text: Part of coat the French friend turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the whole is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A French friend arrives wearing part of a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole of LE plus PAL, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back flap on the front of a coat.

clue.text: Gratuitous error made by some employer

indicators.note: the answer is made by some of the letters of the run of words

explanation.surface: An unnecessary mistake made by a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, so an employer in the literal sense of one who uses.

clue.text: Most uncommon map, perhaps of interest to philatelists

parts.note: rarest means most uncommon

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word might take another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An extremely scarce map that stamp collectors might want.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare stamp is a scarce postage stamp, the prize philatelists seek.

clue.text: Plant found by animal doctor at church

parts.note: a vet treats animals

explanation.surface: A plant discovered by a vet near a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a climbing leguminous plant of the pea family.

clue.text: Express approbation of last rose, perhaps

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word in another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing admiration for the final rose of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or give public support to something.

clue.text: A dog on the prowl?

parts.note: a hunting dog breed, and read literally one who lurks about, a prowler

explanation.surface: A dog roaming about looking for prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, and the word once meant a prowler or petty thief.
